title: Pro-etale extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$

be an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]
and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every complex
$K$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $U_{\Proet}$ the canonical map

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$; here all functors are the
pro-etale ones of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], with inverse image as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and the small sites and constant-coefficient derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

proof.text: First work in the abelian categories of sheaves of modules over the finite constant ring $\Lambda$, rather than taking ordinary direct images of derived objects. The pro-etale inverse-image construction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] provides the morphisms of topoi for $g$ and $g_U$. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], their coefficient structure maps are isomorphisms preserving constant sections; thus the module pullbacks are the $g^{-1}$ and $g_U^{-1}$ of the statement. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to these two morphisms with their constant coefficient sheaves to obtain $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ and $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$. For $j$ and $j'$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the small sites with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ and $X'_{\mathrm{proet}}/U'$ and identifies the restricted coefficient rings with $\Lambda_U$ and $\Lambda_{U'}$. Under these identifications $j^{-1}$ and $j'^{-1}$ are restriction. To verify that the scheme-induced inverse image is this restriction, let $W\to U$ be a site object. It is also an $X$-site object by the localization theorem. In the inverse-image indexing category of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] at $W$, the object $(W,W\to U\times_XW)$ is initial: an object $(V,\phi:W\to U\times_XV)$ determines the unique arrow $W\to V$ over $X$ by projection, and the induced arrow to that object respects $\phi$ since its two projections do. The opposite indexing category has this object terminal, so its presheaf colimit is $F(W\to X)$. These values already form the restriction sheaf, so sheafification does not change them; the coefficient action is the restricted action under the constant-ring identification. For $j'$, an object $W'\to U'$ gives $(W',W'\to U'\times_{X'}W')$ in its inverse-image indexing category. Each $(V',\phi':W'\to U'\times_{X'}V')$ receives the unique arrow from it given by $\operatorname{pr}_{V'}\phi'$; equality of the two projections checks the required compatibility. The opposite-category colimit is therefore $F'(W'\to X')$, a sheaf under restriction, with the restricted coefficient action. These identifications commute with restriction along $W'_1\to W'_2$ because both send a section to its restriction along the composite map to the chosen $V'$; thus they identify functors, not just object values. Therefore [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] gives $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$. Every adjunction in the rest of the sheaf calculation is therefore a module adjunction with the same coefficient ring.

proof.text:
The right-adjoint comparison can be computed on sections without any stalk-conservativity assertion. Write $\iota_j(V\to U)=(V\to U\to X)$ and $\iota_{j'}(V'\to U')=(V'\to U'\to X')$, using [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The chosen cartesian identification $U'\cong U\times_X X'$ in [def-cbc-open-immersion-square] gives, for each $V\to U$, an isomorphism of weakly etale $X'$-objects
$$a_V:V\times_U U'\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_X X'.$$
It sends a pair $(v,u')$ to $(v,j'(u'))$. Conversely, a compatible pair $(v,x')$ determines the unique $u'$ with $g_U(u')$ equal to the image of $v$ in $U$ and $j'(u')=x'$, by the fibre-product universal property; this gives the inverse. The two composites fix both projections, hence are identities. These isomorphisms commute with the maps induced by arrows $V_1\to V_2$ over $U$, since both resulting maps have the same projections. The functor on localized sites obtained by localizing $u_g$ at $U$ is consequently the base-change functor for $g_U$, under the displayed site identifications. The restricted ring structure map of this localized morphism agrees with that for $g_U$: under the restricted constant-ring identifications from step 1, its adjunct sends each constant section $\lambda\in\Lambda$ to the constant section $\lambda$ after base change, exactly as $\rho^{g_U}_\Lambda$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Maps out of the constant presheaf extend uniquely to its sheafification, so these ring maps agree. Hence this identification also identifies the module pushforwards and their scalar actions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to $u_g$ with $V=U$ and $u_g(U)=X'\times_XU\cong U'$. It gives the canonical isomorphism
$$t:j^{-1}g_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{U*}j'^{-1}.$$
Explicitly, for a module sheaf $M$ on $X'_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and restriction give
$$(j^{-1}g_*M)(V)=M(V\times_XX'),\qquad(g_{U*}j'^{-1}M)(V)=M(V\times_UU'),$$
and $t_{M,V}=M(a_V)$, with inverse $M(a_V^{-1})$. This also proves naturality in $M$ and in $V$. Its linearity, including the restricted $\Lambda_U(V)$-action, is part of the ringed localization theorem. In particular we use a canonical natural isomorphism, not strict equality of differently chosen fibre products or small skeleta.

proof.text:
Set $L_1=g^{-1}j_!$, $R_1=j^{-1}g_*$, $L_2=j'_!g_U^{-1}$ and $R_2=g_{U*}j'^{-1}$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and step 1 there are composite adjunctions $L_1\dashv R_1$ and $L_2\dashv R_2$. Their Hom bijections are, respectively,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(g^{-1}j_!F,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!F,g_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,j^{-1}g_*M),$$
$$\operatorname{Hom}(j'_!g_U^{-1}F,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(g_U^{-1}F,j'^{-1}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,g_{U*}j'^{-1}M).$$
Let $\delta=t^{-1}:R_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives a natural isomorphism $\beta:L_1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_2$, characterized by
$$R_1(\beta_F)\circ\eta_{1,F}=\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}.$$
Here the units are those of the displayed composite adjunctions. To specify the comparison, not merely the existence of some isomorphism, its component is explicitly
$$\beta_F=\varepsilon_{1,L_2F}\circ L_1(\delta_{L_2F})\circ L_1(\eta_{2,F}).$$
The adjoint of this map is $\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}$, by the adjunction triangle identity. This is exactly the unit/counit construction of the open extension-by-zero base-change map in the direction of the statement, conjugating the sectionwise cartesian comparison $t^{-1}$. The reverse comparison is
$$\gamma_F=\varepsilon_{2,L_1F}\circ L_2(t_{L_1F})\circ L_2(\eta_{1,F}).$$
The cited conjugation theorem applied in the reverse direction, and its uniqueness under the unit equation, show $\gamma=\beta^{-1}$. Thus the canonical comparison, with this orientation, is invertible and natural in $F$.

proof.text:
For a cochain complex $K$, take in degree $n$ the sheaf isomorphism $\beta_{K^n}$ constructed in step 3. Naturality with respect to $d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1}$ says
$$L_2(d^n)\circ\beta_{K^n}=\beta_{K^{n+1}}\circ L_1(d^n).$$
Consequently these components form a chain map $L_1K\to L_2K$. Naturality of $\gamma$ gives $L_1(d^n)\circ\gamma_{K^n}=\gamma_{K^{n+1}}\circ L_2(d^n)$, so its components form the reverse chain map. The two composites in degree $n$ are $\gamma_{K^n}\circ\beta_{K^n}=\mathrm{id}_{L_1K^n}$ and $\beta_{K^n}\circ\gamma_{K^n}=\mathrm{id}_{L_2K^n}$. Naturality for a map of complexes holds in each degree by step 3. This proves the asserted natural isomorphism on complexes, without any boundedness or constructibility assumption.

source.place: Proof, concluding assertion for complexes; the degreewise chain-map verification is written out here

proof.text: If $K$ is read as an object of the ordinary unbounded derived category, the same comparison applies. The functors $g^{-1}$ and $g_U^{-1}$ on the finite constant-coefficient module sheaves are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]; the functors $j_!$ and $j'_!$ are exact and act degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] each of these termwise functors preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces its exact derived functor, represented by its termwise value on every complex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], clause (2), to the natural chain isomorphisms $\beta$ and $\gamma$ of step 4, composed with the target localization. They descend to inverse natural transformations because their compositions and the identity transformations descend compatibly. This is the same canonical comparison on the derived category, and it is an isomorphism there as well. No ordinary $g_*$ is being substituted for $Rg_*$ in a derived Hom calculation: the right-adjoint argument was completed on sheaves before taking complexes and localizing.
